actions.body: Recent literature in reinforcement learning for healthcare and multimodal systems demonstrates that early exploration trajectories significantly prune future behavioral possibilities. These initial conditions create persistent path-dependent constraints, leading to the formation of stable, emergent preferences. Rather than accidental biases, these structures function as de facto objectives, emerging naturally from the interplay between extrinsic reinforcement and the system's own exploratory history. Further study is required to distinguish between intrinsic curiosity-driven emergence and extrinsic reward-driven stability.
